pr_title: [MVC] Fix global MVC data sources state
pr_body:
# Description

Conventional MVC routes mapped in a router within a branch on the middleware pipeline are also mapped in other branches, and the order for the conventional and dynamic routes is global instead of scoped to a given router middleware.

This change registers a controller and page endpoint data sources per router instead of globally as singletons and makes sure the route order is also done on a "per-router" instance basis.

# Customer Impact
* Endpoints can be reachable from unexpected request paths, which can lead to issues on the application.
* The order of conventional routes can be affected by a change in another branch of the middleware pipeline, which is really hard to detect.

# Regression?

No, this bug was introduced in endpoint routing 3.1 and we will likely patch it (with an AppCompat switch for 3.1)

# Risk

Medium-low. This will alter the way matching works for existing applications that have relied on this behavior, but the same "legacy" behavior can be achieved modifying the startup code, and we don't think the scenario is not common enough for a lot of people to have started unconsciously depending on it.

## Fixes
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/19330

I got pinged on this but I don't really feel like I got the gist of what's being done from the description. 

Is the problem that if you register two endpoint middlewares and wire up different MVC conventional routes you get crosstalk between then because the data source is shared?

What's not clicking for me is why we need caches and custom metadata to solve. What's the *next* problem if you make the data sources non-singleton?

I will admit to not understanding the problem that's being solved 100% ........ but it feels like more complexity is being layered on, when it might be the same that something underlying needs a refactor instead.

I didn't have time yesterday to explain the whole situation and I still had to investigate the impacts on link generation. I've done both now and here are the details:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/25714#issuecomment-691185920

In essence, conventional routes are being matched across branches and the order is global and not per middleware branch, those are the two things this PR aims to fix.

The current changes don't account for link generation, but the details above explain the plan, why it doesn't make the situation any worse than it currently is, and some potential improvements for the future.

Thanks for clarifying, that's much more understandable 👍 

> What's not clicking for me is why we need caches and custom metadata to solve. What's the next problem if you make the data sources non-singleton?

This seems like a real oversight when developing dynamic route value transformer (my fault).  Basically there are two concerns to balance:

- Endpoints and Metadata are **data** - they must not not implement behaviors, and they ideally do not not close over references to services. This is why the endpoint/metadata and **policy** are separate for the dynamic case.
- Matcher policies are stateless, and should operate on the endpoint + metadata to satisfy their inputs.

These are the **rules**. I know that they are good because I made them up 🤣 

Using a cache + ids seems to give the effect of letting the endpoint reference its own data source, while not making that a link that the GC would understand. Would it be better to just bend the rules and say that an endpoint can reference its own data source?

@rynowak thanks for taking a look :)

I agree with your points. I'm focusing now on getting the correct behavior + tests in place since everything else is internal for the most part, I plan to revisit some of these things in 6.0 as part of looking more into link generation.

> Using a cache + ids seems to give the effect of letting the endpoint reference its own data source, while not making that a link that the GC would understand. Would it be better to just bend the rules and say that an endpoint can reference its own data source?

> * Endpoints and Metadata are **data** - they must not not implement behaviors, and they ideally do not not close over references to services. This is why the endpoint/metadata and **policy** are separate for the dynamic case.
> * Matcher policies are stateless, and should operate on the endpoint + metadata to satisfy their inputs.

That's exactly what I was going for with the "id", I could arguably put the DataSource as the endpoint in metadata, but I want to even prevent people from finding it on the collection and casting to it to "party-on", these are very long lived objects (the pipeline only gets built once) and other objects hold on to them for the entire lifetime of the app, so I think the indirection is fine. I can't foresee a scenario in which the metadata id becomes invalid other than the developer specifically poking the collection and removing it, and at that point "we don't care" (since you've gone out of your way to break it).

I still need to cleanup the "caches" code, but in essence they probably don't need to be that complex since they are singletons and when the server stops they will be collectible by the GC.

🆙 📅 

* Addressed feedback
* Added tests
* Included an overload to specify order on dynamic endpoints explicitly.

issue_context.title: When using Map with UseEndpoints, routes are mixed up between pipeline branches
issue_context.body:
### Description
When using `Map` with `UseEndpoints`, all routes are available in all branches.

### To Reproduce
``` C#
public void Configure(IApplicationBuilder app, IWebHostEnvironment env)
{
    app.Map(new PathString("/path1"), builder =>
    {
        builder.UseRouting();
        builder.UseEndpoints(endpoints =>
        {
            endpoints.MapControllerRoute(
                "Route1", "route1",
                defaults: new { controller = "WeatherForecast", action = "Action1" });
        });
    });

    app.Map(new PathString("/path2"), builder =>
    {
        builder.UseRouting();
        builder.UseEndpoints(endpoints =>
        {
            endpoints.MapControllerRoute(
                "Route2", "route2",
                defaults: new { controller = "WeatherForecast", action = "Action2" });
        });
    });
}
```

This should only give me the following two URLs: `/path1/route1` and `/path2/route2`, but if I try `/path1/route2`, `Action2` is called. It should give me 404 instead.

This used to work fine with `UseMvc`.

### Further technical details
